nodes.label: Swatch Library admin
nodes.rationale: Each colour × stone size × backfilm is its own real photo; changes apply on the next render without a deploy.

nodes.label: Crystal Zone Map
nodes.rationale: Minimum feature is ONE stone, not 2.5 — over-boldening destroys the design; only features thinner than one stone are boldened, and anything that cannot survive even that is flagged unmakeable.

nodes.label: printed mode (Mode A)
nodes.rationale: Recommended MVP target: customer artwork is printed under transparent crystals giving arbitrary continuous graphics, the most flexible and impressive first demo, with a material/render path already proven.

nodes.label: Crystal refraction model (Mode A)
nodes.rationale: A graphic printed under transparent crystal is not sharp — each crystal is a tiny lens, so fine lines blur and displace, and bigger stones refract more; a crisp overlay looks fake. Legibility depends on line thickness vs stone size, which becomes a genuine sales aid.

nodes.label: zone_map mode (Mode B)
nodes.rationale: Colour is discrete per stone, so the design is a REGION map quantised onto a jittered per-stone Voronoi grid — the colour boundary must snap to whole stones, giving irregular zig-zag edges, which is essential to realism not optional.

nodes.label: Crystal Fabric Studio — V7.22 Plan
nodes.rationale: The real option model is colour × type × mode, keyed to real photographed swatches — invented option names with no photographic backing were deliberately removed once and must not be reintroduced.

nodes.label: Customizer — Build Plan
nodes.rationale: Render engine runs server-side in Python on Fly.io, reusing the validated numpy/PIL engine; the browser never runs it, and the Netlify edge proxy keeps the Fly.io auth token off the client.

nodes.label: BOM Components
nodes.rationale: ERP figurines can still appear as components in the BOM, but the client-facing item is always the CG code.

nodes.label: CG-[CAT]-[YY][NN] Product Code Convention
nodes.rationale: Always code products; only code components selectively — keeps the system practical, searchable and scalable without making day-to-day data entry too heavy.

nodes.label: client_quotes Collection
nodes.rationale: Snapshots the exchange rate into each quote (rmb_to_hkd_rate) so old quotes remain auditable even after rates change.

nodes.label: CMP-[TYPE]-[DETAIL] Component Code
nodes.rationale: Lightweight and optional — start with no component codes, assign only to high-impact components reused in 3+ products, so existing costing logic stays unchanged.

nodes.label: erp_code ERP Reference
nodes.rationale: Component level continues to use the existing JES/ERP coding system as canonical identifier; the tool stores ERP codes as references without replicating ERP coding logic.

nodes.label: settings/exchange_rates
nodes.rationale: Live rates are shown alongside saved rates but require manual Apply before writing — keeps Finance in control of the rate actually used.

nodes.label: product_code Field
nodes.rationale: Codes are never changed after use in a client quote; a significantly changed concept gets a new code and the old one is marked discontinued or legacy.

nodes.label: V1 PDF Quote Layout Spec
nodes.rationale: Adds a Notes & Conditions section instead of a grand total.

nodes.rationale: Scoring rules with penalties for incompatible lead time, MOQ or budget; returns top N scored items per bucket.

nodes.label: ProductTag Entity

nodes.label: Crystal Fabric Studio

nodes.label: Portal Order / Invoice History
nodes.rationale: Deliberately SI only, not SO/PI (owner: only concern is what is ordered and sold to the customer); a second server-side action re-verifies the invoice's customer_code before returning line items.

nodes.rationale: Featured Products are hand-picked with a chosen photo per product rather than an automatic new/bestseller algorithm, and branded_for_customer_id photos are excluded because the list is public to every customer.

nodes.label: Daily Drafts Re-engagement Engine
nodes.rationale: Summaries are cached on the customer doc and read cheaply by fit-scoring/personalization prompts rather than re-rendering raw threads on every batch run.

nodes.label: Physical Design Workbench
nodes.rationale: Built one workstream at a time with the template library first, because every other workstream needs a real photo+SVG+mm template to work against.

nodes.label: Email Archive / Ingestion Pipeline
nodes.rationale: email-sync and archive_import share one matching/threading/upsert implementation so a thread started in the archive and continued live becomes one Firestore doc.

nodes.label: ERP Incremental Sync
nodes.rationale: A NULL watermark means sync.py builds no WHERE clause and pushes every row through UPSERT, slower than the full load, so watermarks were seeded deliberately before the first incremental run.

nodes.label: JES Retirement Plan
nodes.rationale: Sequence confirmed with owner: production first, then sales orders plus purchase orders together, invoices last, because the books are the one downstream consumer that must not break.

nodes.label: Mailchimp Retirement
nodes.rationale: A mirror snippet ran in parallel first so the two systems coexisted with zero UX change; it was promoted to a full cutover only after the owner cancelled the Mailchimp plan.

nodes.label: marketing_contacts Collection
nodes.rationale: Deliberately separate from customers because some people are in both, and the owner wanted to organise them on his own terms rather than merge on sight.

nodes.label: resend-webhook.js Engagement Tracking
nodes.rationale: Real reply detection is not possible via Resend; replies land as inbound email at sales@uart.com.hk entirely outside Resend, and the webhook says so plainly rather than overselling.

nodes.label: App.jsx Self-Heal Effect
nodes.rationale: Removed entirely rather than patched a third time; a genuinely orphaned Auth account now sits on PendingScreen until a human notices, and the right future fix is a passive admin-visible flag, never another automatic write.

nodes.label: Sensitive-Customer Photo Screening
nodes.rationale: Firestore get()/exists()-based rules reliably gate a single-document get but do not reliably filter collection list()/query results, so privacy screening must also be enforced client-side after the fetch.

nodes.label: 31 March Stock Valuation
nodes.rationale: The audit needs a done-but-not-shipped figure, which can be derived from orders with production-in but not shipped rather than requiring a stored finished-goods balance, keeping the implicit-output decision intact.

nodes.norm_label: su-08 marketing-lead interaction-history audit + two-phase fix

nodes.label: Tag Manager and Tag Cleanup
nodes.rationale: AI proposes merge groups and a canonical spelling but an admin reviews before anything is applied; a legacy value is surfaced as its own option rather than dropped.

nodes.label: UC Registry and Invoice Numbering
nodes.rationale: UC allocation chained to invoice creation removes the duplicate-UC slip caused by duplicating a JES order and forgetting to change the UC by hand.

nodes.label: PDF render harness
nodes.rationale: PDF layout used to be changed blind and caused three bad deploys in one evening; rendering the real component headlessly makes visual breakage obvious.

nodes.label: firestore.rules
nodes.rationale: The real security boundary — the UI is not. Deploys separately from Netlify, rules-first.

nodes.label: storage.rules
nodes.rationale: A separate boundary that MUST track firestore.rules path-for-path.

nodes.label: Customer data isolation (B2B confidentiality)
nodes.rationale: Crystocraft manufactures branded gifts for competing clients; visibility is decided by the deterministic viewerIsSensitive() rule + branded_for_customer_id comparison, never a UI check or an AI judgement.

nodes.norm_label: deterministic boundaries — ai reports observables, code decides

nodes.norm_label: rbac — roles and the multi-file contract

nodes.norm_label: l-01 — admin account silently demoted to pending

nodes.norm_label: l-06 — normline silently drops un-whitelisted line fields

nodes.label: WooCommerce Payments Gateway
nodes.rationale: Gateway fee lives in private post meta (_wcpay_transaction_fee / _wcpay_net); null — not 0 — is returned when neither source has anything so a genuinely missing fee is never misread as no fee charged.

nodes.label: DeepSeek Technical Analysis Prompt
nodes.rationale: Requires clearly labelled confirmed facts, assumptions, open questions and decisions needing Cindy's approval; do not invent accounting or legal rules.

nodes.rationale: Extend the existing invoice/credit-note/UC model rather than build a parallel system; Phase 1 built alone first so real output closes open questions with evidence instead of assumption.

nodes.label: erp_item (materialized view, latest revision per code)
nodes.norm_label: erp_item (materialized view, latest revision per code)
nodes.rationale: Collapses a ~1.4M-row revision history to ~44k rows and is trigram-indexed for fast search; carries costs so the endpoint is admin-only.

nodes.label: explode_bom(code) recursive BOM walk
nodes.rationale: Walks the current BOM for a full multi-level explosion with extended quantities.

nodes.label: erp_readonly SQL login
nodes.rationale: db_datareader only and verified write-blocked — the sync physically cannot modify the ERP.

nodes.label: raw.* — 1:1 text mirror
nodes.rationale: All columns text — ugly but bulletproof against source type/encoding quirks; the app never reads it directly.

nodes.label: uc_registry + uc_seq (app-owned)
nodes.rationale: It is not part of the ERP mirror and is not touched by sync.py — it replaces the Invoice_Check_lists.xls spreadsheet and joins to ERP sales invoices on jes_si.

nodes.label: ERP → Supabase Sync README
nodes.rationale: Deliberately a simple, reliable v1: one-way, read-only, mostly full snapshots, easy to review.

nodes.label: Artgen pipeline — Style → Manifest → Review → Upload
nodes.norm_label: artgen pipeline — style → manifest → review → upload
nodes.rationale: Offline and operator-triggered — MUST NEVER run on a public page visit; nothing reaches WordPress without human sign-off and a manifest record.

nodes.label: Blog → WordPress publishing & SEO
nodes.rationale: Two renderers (preview HTML = design intent; publish-to-wordpress = shipped Gutenberg blocks) must be kept converged — the theme overrides wp:button colours.

nodes.label: Campaigns — batched sends
nodes.rationale: Batch sends are admin-triggered; there is no cron.

nodes.label: Daily Drafts — personalized outreach
nodes.rationale: A draft memory rule that steers every future draft starts pending and needs a second, explicit approval — nothing goes live off one click.

nodes.label: Product Truth — the immutable hard rule
nodes.norm_label: product truth — the immutable hard rule
nodes.rationale: Test: could a reasonable customer ask for its price/SKU? If yes and it isn't a real catalogue product the image is a failure — abstract editorial art only.

nodes.label: Badge Component
nodes.rationale: Keep badge text short — 1–3 words; zero border-radius for major contexts.

nodes.label: Button Component
nodes.rationale: Uppercase, ultra-wide-tracked, zero border-radius — references the geometric wordmark's letter-spacing; never playful, always precise.

nodes.label: Tag Component
nodes.rationale: Rounder than Badge; interactive when onClick is provided, used for filter chips in horizontal scrollable rows.

nodes.label: Card Component
nodes.rationale: Square corners are the Crystocraft signature; flat by default with a whisper of elevation only on hover or genuinely floating surfaces.

nodes.label: TrustSeal Component
nodes.rationale: Monochrome by default so it survives engraving, embossing and one-colour print; system rule is max one authentication seal plus one heritage seal per item.

nodes.label: Input Component
nodes.rationale: Underline variant default gives a premium, editorial feel; boxed variant for denser form layouts.

nodes.label: Select Component
nodes.rationale: Custom arrow icon matches the brand's geometric vocabulary.

nodes.label: Logo Lockups Card
nodes.rationale: Three-tier usage system: large format, small (<1cm), micro (<5mm) where the ® and butterfly detail are suppressed.

nodes.label: Radius & Shadows Card
nodes.rationale: Hairline-first — drop shadows used sparingly, elevation reserved for floating surfaces.

nodes.label: Headings — Questrial Card
nodes.rationale: H1–H3 uppercase, H4 normal case.

nodes.label: Eyebrow / Kicker Card
nodes.rationale: The signature label — its colour signals the division (Bronze / Sapphire / Burgundy).

nodes.label: Bespoke Gifting Hub Template
nodes.rationale: Burgundy-accented corporate site with four-step process, portfolio grid and brief submission form.

nodes.label: Blog Article Template
nodes.rationale: Editorial heritage and craft storytelling layout with spec callout, pull quote and related articles.

nodes.label: Product Catalogue Template
nodes.rationale: Filterable grid with product detail overlay modal.

nodes.label: Crystals Hub Template
nodes.rationale: Sapphire-accented specification catalogue with interactive detail panel and trade enquiry CTA.

nodes.label: Gifts Hub Template
nodes.rationale: Flagship consumer site with product grid, category filters, heritage strip and product detail modal.

nodes.label: Badge
nodes.rationale: Divisions variants mark cross-listed content; keep badge text short (1-3 words).

nodes.label: Button
nodes.rationale: Uppercase, ultra-wide-tracked, zero border-radius to reference the geometric wordmark's letter-spacing; never playful.

nodes.label: Tag
nodes.rationale: Pill-shaped and rounder than Badge; interactive when onClick is provided, for filter chips and collection labels.

nodes.label: Card
nodes.rationale: Square corners (0 border-radius) are the Crystocraft signature; flat by default with hairlines doing the separating.

nodes.label: TrustSeal
nodes.rationale: Monochrome by default so it survives engraving, embossing, and one-colour print; max one authentication plus one heritage seal per item to avoid looking cheap.

nodes.label: Input
nodes.rationale: Underline variant default gives a premium, editorial feel; boxed variant is for denser form layouts.

nodes.label: Select
nodes.rationale: Underline default is best for clean single-page enquiry forms; boxed for dense or card-surface layouts.

nodes.label: Bespoke Gifting Hub Template
nodes.rationale: Corporate hub runs brief -> render -> finished sequence with an enquiry form that is the front end of UA-ProductManager.

nodes.label: Blog Article Template
nodes.rationale: Blog stays a shared content engine; high-traffic Swarovski-alternative posts link directly to the Crystals enquiry to shorten traffic-to-revenue.

nodes.label: Crystals Hub Template
nodes.rationale: B2B hub keeps sapphire sparingly, uses tabular spec tables and technical callouts; doubles as content engine and Swarovski-alternative proof.

nodes.label: Gifts Hub Template
nodes.rationale: Flagship consumer hub uses the Gifts accent and a serif-led, editorial, object-forward treatment.

nodes.label: Bespoke Proposal Template
nodes.rationale: Formal client proposal document using CraftNote annotations and a signed agreement to authorise production.

nodes.label: Crystocraft Bespoke Gifting Division
nodes.rationale: Burgundy accent — the most direct and efficient division; fast, at any scale, managed end-to-end.

nodes.label: Crystocraft Crystals Division
nodes.rationale: Sapphire accent used sparingly — lots of ink, ivory and white space; restraint signals a serious manufacturer.

nodes.label: Crystocraft Gifts Division
nodes.rationale: Bronze Gold accent — warm, celebratory, the most editorial division.

nodes.label: Questrial Typeface
nodes.rationale: Geometric monoline sans that echoes the wordmark's construction; H1–H3 uppercase weight 400, single weight only.

nodes.label: Work Sans Typeface
nodes.rationale: Carries the wide-tracked caps for eyebrow labels, captions, badges and buttons; tabular figures for aligned spec numbers in the Crystals division.

nodes.label: Brand Truth — Masters Metal and Crystal In-House
nodes.norm_label: brand truth — masters metal and crystal in-house
nodes.rationale: Quality kept alive when the rest of the market chased cost; the metal story and crystal story share one arc.

nodes.label: Dazzle Crystal Cut
nodes.rationale: A product technology (not a sub-brand); 32 facets snowflake-inspired, distributed to spread light evenly rather than fewer coarse facets.

nodes.label: Crystocraft Gifts Division (Flagship)
nodes.rationale: Carries no descriptor — it is the default face and wears the signature line.

nodes.label: Light Is the Hero (Art Direction)
nodes.rationale: Authenticity is the entire premise of a craft brand, so real photography is used for product and craft while AI is reserved for context and customisation previews.

nodes.label: Fixed Butterfly Logo Lockup
nodes.rationale: Mark is trademarked and never modified; primary lockup is single-colour so it survives engraving, embossing, foil, and one-colour print.

nodes.label: Trust Seals System
nodes.rationale: Replaces the reassurance buyers lost when Swarovski withdrew its swan hangtag and certificate; seal earns attention, certificate earns the order.

nodes.label: UA-ProductManager
nodes.rationale: Internal-only workflow application; B2B enquiry forms are its front end, and a fast polished response is the brand promise.

nodes.label: Crystocraft Design System (v2-2026 readme)
nodes.rationale: Branded house — one master brand, three divisions differentiated by descriptor only; the accent colour is the only thing that changes between divisions.

nodes.label: Crystocraft Brand Guidelines
nodes.rationale: Built to be handed to designers, developers, and suppliers as one source of truth.

nodes.label: Crystocraft Brand Identity for Design System V2
nodes.norm_label: crystocraft brand identity for design system v2

nodes.label: Crystocraft Design System README
nodes.rationale: No Figma file or codebase was provided, so all design decisions are derived from the brand guidelines document.

nodes.label: Crystocraft Design Skill
nodes.rationale: Skill entry point that points the agent at the README and available files so it can act as a brand expert.

nodes.label: Butterfly Mark / Logo Lockup
nodes.rationale: Never modified, monochrome always — accents appear only in the system around the logo, never inside the mark.

nodes.label: Product Code / Image Filename Mapping
nodes.rationale: Manifest maps each missing image filename to one or more ERP product codes, with a count column indicating number of codes matched; multiple or repeated codes signal ambiguous or dirty SKU data.

nodes.label: Inventory Images Missing Manifest
nodes.rationale: Tab-separated list of missing image filenames, an occurrence count, and the associated item/SKU codes; used to reconcile product imagery against the ERP item catalog.

nodes.label: Google Analytics 4 (G-HRTV0QWTNG)
nodes.rationale: Enhanced measurement (default on) tracks History API navigation automatically, so SPA route changes are picked up without custom React Router wiring.

nodes.label: Alibaba Messages manual-paste enrichment
nodes.rationale: Alibaba.com offers no export for buyer-seller chat, so manual paste is the only route in; the card is always visible because pasting IS how content gets in.

nodes.label: Crystal Fabric Customizer — Proof of Concept
nodes.norm_label: crystal fabric customizer — proof of concept
nodes.rationale: Deterministic no-AI render: identical every run, milliseconds, no generative AI — capture the crystal material once from a real swatch photo and composite the design through it.

nodes.label: crystal_swatch_notes collection
nodes.rationale: Holds only the metadata that has no other home (recommended use-cases, legacy Swarovski refs); read opened to approved customers because the legacy-reference list only has a point if a designer can see it, writes stay admin-only.

nodes.label: customers/{id}/assets Brand Gallery subcollection
nodes.rationale: Nested subcollection makes the security rule trivial and correct; visibility (who can see it) and can_use_in_marketing (may we promote with it) are deliberately separate flags, and upload defaults are conservative so nothing leaks until an admin opens it.

nodes.label: Per-User Module Access (admin/staff/customer)
nodes.rationale: Sensitive module keys grant sight of costs, margins, all-customer data or money, so the admin owns not mis-ticking them.

nodes.label: Reserve → Produce-in → Release Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Components are reserved at order confirmation + deposit and only produced-in/committed later when actually built into finished goods, so Available (not raw on-hand) drives the buildable promise.

nodes.label: Crystocraft Operation Center — orientation
nodes.rationale: This file is the map, not the content — it points to the docs/skills/ system rather than duplicating it.

nodes.label: Customer Brand Gallery & Logo Privacy — Spec
nodes.norm_label: customer brand gallery & logo privacy — spec
nodes.rationale: This is the specific thing that unblocks inviting corporate customers to log in: a client's logo must never appear in the public catalogue, the blog, or another customer's view, and must be usable in that client's own proposal with one click.

nodes.label: Operation Center — Master Index (moved)
nodes.rationale: The index moved into the skill system so there is now one system, not two; the old file is kept so old links resolve.

nodes.label: Local tooling already available
nodes.rationale: This file is checked into git so it survives across the two-Mac sync; read it before telling the user how to install something.

nodes.label: RBAC Flexible Per-User Module Access Plan
nodes.norm_label: rbac flexible per-user module access plan
nodes.rationale: Drop the fixed production/sales staff roles; every account becomes admin, staff, or customer, with staff carrying an explicit modules[] list toggled by the admin.

nodes.label: Editable Reserved Quantity Feasibility Audit
nodes.rationale: Today the only way to change a reserved quantity is to release the whole reservation and redo it; this audit designs an in-place edit primitive shared by all three stock classes.

nodes.label: TECH-DEBT
nodes.rationale: A running list of things noticed in passing — not urgent bugs, not fixed silently, recorded so they don't get rediscovered from scratch.

nodes.label: src/index.css
nodes.rationale: @layer base / @layer components holds the authoritative .btn*, .input, .card, .tag, .badge, .label, .eyebrow, .mosaic-* rules.

nodes.label: src/index.css (@layer base / components)
nodes.rationale: Token values are hand-copied in so tokens don't depend on a dev-server restart.

nodes.label: Three divisions, one master brand
nodes.rationale: The accent colour is the sole visual cue that differentiates Gifts (Bronze Gold), Crystals (Sapphire) and Bespoke (Burgundy) — everything else is shared.

nodes.label: Light is the hero
nodes.rationale: Every design decision should serve 'light caught by craftsmanship' — sparkle off crystal facets, glints off mirror-finish metal, controlled not decorative.

nodes.label: Logo — single-colour lockup rule
nodes.rationale: Accent colours live in the surrounding system, never inside the mark; the trademarked butterfly + wordmark is fixed and never redrawn.

nodes.label: Token layer — colour ramps, type, spacing, elevation, radius
nodes.norm_label: token layer — colour ramps, type, spacing, elevation, radius
nodes.rationale: Square by default and flat: a resting card has no shadow, only a 1px warm-grey hairline.

nodes.label: Design system SSOT — tailwind.config.js + index.css
nodes.rationale: The exported bundles are not imported; there is no colors.css/spacing.css the app reads.

nodes.label: docs/skills/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md (V3 target)
nodes.rationale: Any V3 work starts by writing the spec of what V2.5 actually is, extracted from the config and CSS, then deciding the deltas.

nodes.label: Crystocraft Design System — Reference Exports README
nodes.norm_label: crystocraft design system — reference exports readme
nodes.rationale: Bundles are reference material only; the authoritative design system is tailwind.config.js + src/index.css, with token values hand-copied rather than @import-ed so tokens don't depend on a dev-server restart.

nodes.label: docs/skills/UI-POLISH.md
nodes.rationale: The written companion — visual language, the Second-Pass checklist, §7 Mobile.

nodes.label: src/access.js (MODULE_GROUPS + canAccess)
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth driving both the sidebar filter and the route guards so a hidden menu item can never point at a still-live URL; AccessContext defaults to 'admin' deliberately so a provider-less render fails open rather than white-screening, since the rules are the boundary regardless.

nodes.label: App.jsx (router + gates)
nodes.rationale: The self-heal useEffect that auto-created users/{uid} docs was removed entirely rather than patched again, because a live onSnapshot 'missing' signal is not trustworthy for something that destructive.

nodes.label: lib/auth.js requireModule
nodes.rationale: Takes a string or an array because several AI/OCR-assist functions are only reachable from more than one module; the mechanical migration had over-restricted them to quotes, killing features for the staff meant to use them.
